<p>A <b>horse</b> is a <a href="/w/Passive_mob" class="mw-redirect" title="Passive mob">passive mob</a> that can be <a href="/w/Ridden" class="mw-redirect" title="Ridden">ridden</a> when <a href="/w/Tamed" class="mw-redirect" title="Tamed">tamed</a> and <a href="/w/Saddle" title="Saddle">saddled</a>, and can wear <a href="/w/Horse_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Horse armor">horse armor</a>. Different horses have different running speeds, jump heights, and health points, and these attributes can be inherited and improved through <a href="/w/Breeding" title="Breeding">breeding</a>.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Spawning">Spawning</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=1&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Spawning" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section's source code: Spawning"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>

Notice the same color but different markings.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Horses spawn in <a href="/w/Plains" title="Plains">plains</a> and <a href="/w/Savanna" title="Savanna">savannas</a> in herds of 2–6. For horses, all combinations of color and markings are equally likely. All members of the herd have the same color, but markings may vary. 20% of all individual horses spawn as babies. In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, all individual horses spawn as adults when using spawn eggs.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/w/Village" title="Village">Villages</a> naturally generate with stables and animal pens containing horses.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Appearance">Appearance</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=2&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Appearance" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section's source code: Appearance"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:HorseBreeds.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/HorseBreeds.png/300px-HorseBreeds.png?2fd0e" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="169" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/HorseBreeds.png/600px-HorseBreeds.png?2fd0e 2x" data-file-width="1920" data-file-height="1081"></a><figcaption>All 35 colorations of horses. Base colors, from left to right: white, creamy, chestnut, brown, black, gray, and dark brown. Markings, from bottom to top: none, white stockings and blaze, white field, white spots, and black dots.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Each horse variant has unique features and markings, and a foal. Adult horses are 1.4 blocks wide and long, and 1.6 blocks high. Foals start at half the size of adults. Unlike <a href="/w/Wolves" class="mw-redirect" title="Wolves">wolves</a> and <a href="/w/Cats" class="mw-redirect" title="Cats">cats</a>, horses do not change appearance once they have been tamed, although tamed horses may be differentiated by giving them equipment.
</p><p>Horses can have 1 of 7 base colors: white, creamy, chestnut, brown, black, gray, and dark brown; and 1 of 5 marking patterns: <i>no markings</i>, <i>white stockings and blaze</i>, <i>white field</i>, <i>white spots</i> and <i>black dots</i>. In total, there are 35 possible horse coat combinations.
</p>

<li><a href="/w/Horse_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Horse armor">Horse armor</a> if the horse was already equipped</li>
<li><a href="/w/Saddle" title="Saddle">Saddle</a> if the horse was already equipped.</li></ul>
<p>Killing a foal yields neither items nor experience.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Behavior">Behavior</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=6&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Behavior" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section's source code: Behavior"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Horse_eating_grass.gif" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Horse_eating_grass.gif/300px-Horse_eating_grass.gif?f29ff" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="300" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Horse_eating_grass.gif/600px-Horse_eating_grass.gif?f29ff 2x" data-file-width="1000" data-file-height="1000"></a><figcaption>A horse eating grass.</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Horse_Standing.gif" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Horse_Standing.gif/180px-Horse_Standing.gif?cab0c" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="180" height="150" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Horse_Standing.gif/360px-Horse_Standing.gif?cab0c 2x" data-file-width="500" data-file-height="416"></a><figcaption>A horse rearing.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Horses wander aimlessly, occasionally stopping to rear, flick their tails, or lower their heads as though eating the grass. Unlike <a href="/w/Sheep" title="Sheep">sheep</a>, the eating animation does not actually cause any grass to be consumed. If a player comes near, the horses may turn to look at them. Any horse, even a wild or undead horse, can be attached to a <a href="/w/Lead" title="Lead">lead</a> without protest. Horses remain passive, even when hit.
</p><p>Horses make neighing and whinnying sounds.
</p><p>Baby horses can ride in <a href="/w/Boat" title="Boat">boats</a>, but adults cannot unless commands are used to put them there. If a baby horse in a boat grows up in <i>Java Edition</i>, it dismounts, but in <i>Bedrock Edition</i>, it remains in the boat. Horses can only ride in <a href="/w/Minecart" title="Minecart">minecarts</a> in <i>Bedrock Edition</i>.
</p><p>Horses can safely fall 7 blocks before they begin to accumulate <a href="/w/Fall_damage" class="mw-redirect" title="Fall damage">fall damage</a>, unlike most mobs, which can only safely fall 3 blocks. Horses also take half of the normal fall damage (rounded down) that most other mobs take (0.5<span class="hidden-alt-text">HP</span><span class="nowrap mc-hearts"><span class="iconbar pixel-image nowrap" style="--icon-offset:-1px;" title="1 heart"><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="❤️" src="/images/Heart_%28icon%29.png?faf83" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="9" height="9" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="9" data-file-height="9"></span></span></span> × 0.25</span> damage per block over the safe distance instead of 1<span class="hidden-alt-text">HP</span><span class="nowrap mc-hearts"><span class="iconbar pixel-image nowrap" style="--icon-offset:-1px;" title="0.5 hearts"><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="💔" src="/images/Half_Heart_%28icon%29.png?cb16e" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="9" height="9" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="9" data-file-height="9"></span></span></span></span>). If an entity is riding a horse, they take fall damage as normal, counting from the entity's safe fall distance; however, they also safely fall 7 blocks without taking damage.
</p><p>Horses have a <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>900</sub> chance to regenerate 1<span class="hidden-alt-text">HP</span><span class="nowrap mc-hearts"><span class="iconbar pixel-image nowrap" style="--icon-offset:-1px;" title="0.5 hearts"><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="💔" src="/images/Half_Heart_%28icon%29.png?cb16e" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="9" height="9" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="9" data-file-height="9"></span></span></span></span> health point each game tick.
</p><p>Horses can be led by a player holding a <a href="/w/Golden_carrot" class="mw-redirect" title="Golden carrot">golden carrot</a>, <a href="/w/Golden_apple" class="mw-redirect" title="Golden apple">golden apple</a>, or <a href="/w/Enchanted_golden_apple" class="mw-redirect" title="Enchanted golden apple">enchanted golden apple</a>. Foals follow adult horses. 
</p><p>A horse with a rider can be pulled by a lead, and can even be lifted into the air.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Taming">Taming</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=7&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Taming" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section's source code: Taming"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Taming a horse is required to breed it, to give it equipment, or to control it while riding.
</p><p>In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, a player mounts a horse by pressing <span class="explain" title="Defaults to right click on mouse or left trigger on controller.">use</span> on it <i>with an empty hand</i>. In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, the player can also hold an object that cannot be used on a horse. An adult horse can be tamed by repeatedly mounting it until the horse stops bucking the player off. Taming depends on the horse's "temper". Horses begin with a temper of 0 out of 100. When a player first mounts the horse, a random taming threshold 0–99 is chosen. The horse becomes tame if the temper exceeds this threshold. Otherwise, the player is bucked off and the temper is increased by 5, to be compared against the threshold the next time the player mounts the horse. Temper can also be increased by feeding the horse.
</p><p>After repeated mountings, hearts appear above the horse, indicating that it is tamed.
</p><p>In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, like all tame animals, a death message is displayed to every player when a horse is killed.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Breeding_2">Breeding</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=8&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Breeding" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section's source code: Breeding"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Feeding two tamed horses <a href="/w/Golden_apple" class="mw-redirect" title="Golden apple">golden apples</a> or <a href="/w/Golden_carrot" class="mw-redirect" title="Golden carrot">golden carrots</a> activates <a href="/w/Love_mode" class="mw-redirect" title="Love mode">love mode</a>, causing them to mate and produce a foal. The foal appears more spindly than adult horses. The foal can be fed to make it mature faster.
</p><p>Depending on the variations of the parent horses, the offspring can be one of several types. 
</p>
<ul><li>Bred with a horse: <a href="/w/Breeding" title="Breeding">breeding</a> two horses produces a foal. Usually, the new foal has the color and markings of one of its parents, although there is a <sup>13</sup>⁄<sub>45</sub> chance of having a random color/markings (which may still end up being the same as one of the parents).</li>
<li>Bred with a <a href="/w/Donkey" title="Donkey">donkey</a>: cross-breeding a horse with a donkey creates a baby <a href="/w/Mule" title="Mule">mule</a>. Mules cannot breed. This unlocks the <a href="/w/Artificial_Selection" class="mw-redirect" title="Artificial Selection">Artificial Selection</a> achievement.‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">Bedrock Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup></li></ul>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Food">Food</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=9&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Food" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=9" title="Edit section's source code: Food"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Feeding a horse food can alter its behavior, increase its temper (if untamed), cause it to grow (if it is not yet an adult; foals normally take 20 minutes to fully mature if not fed), and/or restore its health.
</p><p>Only living horses can be fed. Undead variants like <a href="/w/Zombie_Horse" title="Zombie Horse">zombie</a> and <a href="/w/Skeleton_Horse" title="Skeleton Horse">skeleton</a> horses cannot be fed. 
</p><p>The table below lists the effects of the various foods horses can eat.
</p><p>To feed a horse, hold a valid food item and press <span class="explain" title="Defaults to right click on mouse or left trigger on controller.">use</span> on the horse.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Statistics">Statistics</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=11&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Statistics" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=11" title="Edit section's source code: Statistics"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">See also: <a href="/w/Tutorial:Horses" title="Tutorial:Horses">Tutorial:Horses</a> 
</div>
<p>All horses have three "equine stats" that vary from horse to horse: health, (maximum) movement speed, and jump height. These stats are created once the horse is born or spawned, and are not affected by food.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Spawned_values">Spawned values</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=12&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Spawned values" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=12" title="Edit section's source code: Spawned values"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>When spawned in any way except breeding – for instance, using commands, spawning naturally, or using spawn eggs – horses are assigned their stats within certain ranges.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Movement_speed">Movement speed</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=14&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Movement speed" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=14" title="Edit section's source code: Movement speed"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>A horse's movement speed ranges from 0.1125–0.3375 in internal units, with an average of 0.225. For reference, the player's normal walking speed is 0.1. The speed listed does not include any <a href="/w/Status_effect" class="mw-redirect" title="Status effect">status effect</a> that affects the speed of the horse or the player.
</p><p>The conversion factor between internal units and blocks/sec is roughly 43.17, putting the best horse's maximum speed at about 14.57 blocks/second, and the average horse's speed at about 9.71 blocks/sec.
</p>
<ul><li>Minimum: 4.86 blocks/sec.</li>
<li>Player speed (walking): 4.317 blocks/sec.</li>
<li>Player speed (sprinting): 5.612 blocks/sec.</li></ul>
<p>See also <i><a href="/w/Transportation#Methods" title="Transportation">transportation methods</a></i> to compare the speeds of various transportation methods.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Jump_strength">Jump strength</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=15&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Jump strength" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=15" title="Edit section's source code: Jump strength"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Horse's jump strength ranges from 0.4–1.0, with an average of 0.7 in internal units.
</p><p>The minimum jump strength of 0.4 is enough to clear 1.153 blocks, while the maximum of 1.0 is enough to clear 5.9197 blocks. The calculation, however, is not linear with the average jump strength of 0.7 favoring the lower side with the value of 3.124 blocks.<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Bred_values">Bred values</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=16&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Bred values" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=16" title="Edit section's source code: Bred values"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>When breeding two horses, or a horse and a donkey, the baby's stats are determined by the following formula, run for each stat individually:
</p>
<ol><li>Get the absolute difference of the attribute value of both parents</li>
<li>Add 30% of the total value range to the result of step one</li>
<li>Compute a value between -0.5 and 0.5 (the distribution is not equally likely)</li>
<li>Multiply the result of step two with the random value from step three</li>
<li>Add the average of the two parents' attribute values to the result</li></ol>
<p>If the resulting value is
</p>
<ul><li>greater than the allowed maximum,</li>
<li>or smaller than the allowed minimum,</li></ul>
<p>the difference towards that allowed extreme is respectively subtracted/added from/to the value.
</p><p>Although the game performs these operations on the internal attribute values, they can just as well be applied to the in-game values for movement speed and jump height.
</p><p>
A pseudocode implementation might look like this, wherein <code>MIN</code> and <code>MAX</code> represent the extremes Minecraft allows the attribute to assume. Additionally, <code>x</code> and <code>y</code> represent the values the parents hold.</p><div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-python mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr"><pre><span></span><span class="n">base</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="o">|</span> <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">-</span> <span class="n">y</span> <span class="o">|</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="n">MAX</span> <span class="o">-</span> <span class="n">MIN</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="mf">0.3</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="p">((</span><span class="n">rand</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">rand</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">rand</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">))</span> <span class="o">/</span> <span class="mi">3</span> <span class="o">-</span> <span class="mf">0.5</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">y</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">/</span> <span class="mi">2</span>
<span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">base</span> <span class="o">></span> <span class="n">MAX</span><span class="p">:</span>
    <span class="n">base</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">2</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">MAX</span> <span class="o">-</span> <span class="n">base</span>
<span class="k">if</span> <span class="n">base</span> <span class="o"><</span> <span class="n">MIN</span><span class="p">:</span>
    <span class="n">base</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">2</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">MIN</span> <span class="o">-</span> <span class="n">base</span>
<span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">base</span>
</pre></div><p><sup id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-5"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>A foal has an 11% chance to be a random base color and a 20% chance to have random markings. Otherwise, it chooses the values from one of its parents.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Usage">Usage</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=17&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Usage" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=17" title="Edit section's source code: Usage"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">See also: <a href="/w/Transportation" title="Transportation">Transportation</a> 
</div>
<p>Tamed and <a href="/w/Saddle" title="Saddle">saddled</a> horses can be used as a means of <a href="/w/Transportation" title="Transportation">transportation</a>. When ridden, they are able to move faster and jump higher than a normal player. Horses can be used to climb hills and jump fences, as some can jump high enough to clear up to five block heights, versus the player's maximum of about one (without jump boost).
</p><p>Horses can be pulled along and tied up using a <a href="/w/Lead" title="Lead">lead</a>. They can be towed behind a <a href="/w/Boat" title="Boat">boat</a> by using a lead. 
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Equipment">Equipment</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=18&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Equipment" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=18" title="Edit section's source code: Equipment"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Horse_GUI.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Horse_GUI.png/300px-Horse_GUI.png?f29a1" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="283" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/Horse_GUI.png?f29a1 2x" data-file-width="352" data-file-height="332"></a><figcaption>Horse UI</figcaption></figure>
<p>Tamed horses have two equipment slots:
</p>
<ul><li><span class="sprite-file" style="height:32px;width:32px;--vertical-align:middle"><span class="pixel-image" typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="SlotSprite Saddle.png: Sprite image for Saddle in Minecraft" src="/images/SlotSprite_Saddle.png?c43d3" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="32" height="32" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="32" data-file-height="32"></span></span></span> Saddle slot: for equipping a <a href="/w/Saddle" title="Saddle">saddle</a>.</li>
<li><span class="sprite-file" style="height:32px;width:32px;--vertical-align:middle"><span class="pixel-image" typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="SlotSprite Horse Armor.png: Sprite image for Horse Armor in Minecraft" src="/images/SlotSprite_Horse_Armor.png?8eca1" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="32" height="32" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="32" data-file-height="32"></span></span></span> Horse armor slot: for equipping <a href="/w/Horse_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Horse armor">horse armor</a>.</li></ul>
<p>Foals cannot be equipped, as they cannot be ridden.
</p><p>Equipment can be placed on a horse by holding it and then <span class="explain" title="Defaults to right click on mouse or left trigger on controller.">using</span> on the horse, or by accessing its inventory. A horse’s inventory can be accessed by mounting the horse and using <span class="explain" title="Defaults to E on keyboard or top button on right side of controller.">inventory</span> control, or by <span class="explain" title="Defaults to shift on keyboard or right button on the right side of controller.">sneaking</span> and then <span class="explain" title="Defaults to right click on mouse or left trigger on controller.">using</span> or pressing the "open inventory" button‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">Bedrock Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> on the horse. The player cannot open their inventory while on an untamed horse, though they can open containers.
</p><p>The equipment can be removed by two methods:
</p>
<ul><li>Removing the equipment from their slots in the horse's inventory.</li>
<li><span class="explain" title="Defaults to right click on mouse or left trigger on controller.">Using</span> <a href="/w/Shears" title="Shears">shears</a> on the horse. If both a saddle and horse armor are equipped, they are removed one at a time. The first use removes the horse armor, and a second use removes the saddle.</li></ul>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Riding">Riding</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Horse?section=19&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Riding" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Horse?action=edit&section=19" title="Edit section's source code: Riding"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Riding" title="Riding">Riding</a></div>
<p>Once a horse is tamed and saddled, the player can control it with standard directional controls, <span class="explain" title="Defaults to space bar on keyboard or bottom button on right side of controller.">jump</span>, and the mouse. The player dismounts using the <span class="explain" title="Defaults to shift on keyboard or right button on the right side of controller.">dismount</span> control. Like riding other entities, it is impossible for a player to use a <a href="/w/Nether_portal" class="mw-redirect" title="Nether portal">nether portal</a> or <a href="/w/End_portal" title="End portal">end portal</a> while on a horse.‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">Bedrock Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup>
</p><p>A ridden saddled horse automatically runs up any one block high slope. The horse and rider can safely fit through a space as low as 2.75 blocks high. Lower clearance risks suffocating the rider if the rider's head enters a non-transparent block. The horse itself can enter gaps as low as 1.625 blocks high, but may itself take suffocation damage when clearance is less than 1.75 blocks. Horses cannot fit through a 1-block-wide gap.
</p><p>The maximum speed of horses varies between 4.86 blocks/second and 14.57 blocks/second (compared to the player's walking speed, which is about 4.317 blocks/second). About 82% of horses are able to go faster than a minecart. Horses move backward slowly, about as fast as the player when moving sideways. A horse’s speed can also be affected by potions. Speed has no relation to a horse’s outward appearance. However, how fast a horse walks on its own while not being ridden can be an indication of its Speed. This can be useful to determine whether or not a horse is fast without first having to tame it.
</p><p>A ridden saddled horse can be made to <span class="explain" title="Defaults to space bar on keyboard or bottom button on right side of controller.">jump</span> by pressing the jump control. Holding the jump control fills a jump charge bar allowing for a higher jump when released relative to how much the bar was filled. In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, when the player rides a horse, the experience bar on <a href="/w/HUD" class="mw-redirect" title="HUD">HUD</a> is replaced by a jump bar and the player's hunger bar is replaced by the horse's health bar. In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, the player's health bar and hunger bar are displayed while riding a horse and the player's experience bar is replaced by the horse's jump bar when the jump control is activated. During the jump control activation the number denoting the player's experience level is still displayed above the jump bar. If a horse has the jump boost effect, it will not multiply the jump but will increase the maximum jump height, however horses are not affected by jump boost beacons, the effect must be applied by potions or commands. When a player's gravity attribute is higher or lower than the default the player will automatically be dismounted upon jumping or upon landing a jump.
</p>

<p>Horses have entity data associated with them that contain various properties.
</p><p><i><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">Java Edition</a></i>:
</p>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Entity_format" title="Entity format">Entity format</a></div>
<div class="treeview">
<ul><li><span title="NBT Compound / JSON Object"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-48px -16px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[NBT Compound / JSON Object]</span></span> Entity data
<ul><li class="mw-empty-elt"></li><li class="treeview-header nbttree-inherited load-page" data-page="Template:Nbt inherit/breedable/template" data-template="true" data-treeview="true" data-treeviewclass="nbttree-inherited">Additional fields for mobs that can breed<span class="noscript"> see <a href="/w/Template:Nbt_inherit/breedable/template" title="Template:Nbt inherit/breedable/template">Template:Nbt inherit/breedable/template</a></span></li>
<li class="mw-empty-elt"></li><li class="treeview-header nbttree-inherited load-page" data-page="Template:Nbt inherit/entity/template" data-template="true" data-treeview="true" data-treeviewclass="nbttree-inherited">Tags common to all entities<span class="noscript"> see <a href="/w/Template:Nbt_inherit/entity/template" title="Template:Nbt inherit/entity/template">Template:Nbt inherit/entity/template</a></span></li>
<li class="mw-empty-elt"></li><li class="treeview-header nbttree-inherited load-page" data-page="Template:Nbt inherit/mob/template" data-template="true" data-treeview="true" data-treeviewclass="nbttree-inherited">Tags common to all mobs<span class="noscript"> see <a href="/w/Template:Nbt_inherit/mob/template" title="Template:Nbt inherit/mob/template">Template:Nbt inherit/mob/template</a></span></li>
<li><span title="Byte"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-0px -0px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[Byte]</span></span><span class="nowrap" style="font-weight: bold;"> Bred</span>: 1 or 0 (true/false) – Unknown. Remains 0 after breeding. If true, causes it to stay near other horses with this flag set.</li>
<li><span title="Byte"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-0px -0px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[Byte]</span></span><span class="nowrap" style="font-weight: bold;"> EatingHaystack</span>: 1 or 0 (true/false) – true if the mob is eating grass.</li>
<li><span title="Int Array"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-16px -32px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[Int Array]</span></span><span class="nowrap" style="font-weight: bold;"> Owner</span>: The <a href="/w/UUID" title="UUID">UUID</a> of the entity that tamed the mob, stored as four ints. Has no effect on behavior. Does not exist if there is no owner.</li>
<li><span title="Byte"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-0px -0px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[Byte]</span></span><span class="nowrap" style="font-weight: bold;"> Tame</span>: 1 or 0 (true/false) – true if the mob is tamed.</li>
<li><span title="Int"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-48px -0px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[Int]</span></span><span class="nowrap" style="font-weight: bold;"> Temper</span>: Ranges from 0 to 100; increases with feeding. Higher values make a mob easier to tame.</li>
<li><span title="Int"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-48px -0px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[Int]</span></span><span class="nowrap" style="font-weight: bold;"> Variant</span>: The variant and markings of the horse. Encoded as <code>variant | (markings << 8)</code>. Unused values lead to white horses. The encoded variant field represents the <a href="/w/Data_component_format#horse/variant" title="Data component format"><code>minecraft:horse/variant</code></a> component.</li></ul></li></ul>

<p>Variant names taken from the names of the texture file they correspond to.
</p><p>Summoning a horse without specifying the Variant value results in a white horse. Summoning a horse with a correct color byte but an incorrect marking byte results in a horse of the corresponding color but no markings. Summoning a horse with a correct marking byte but an incorrect color byte results in a white horse with the corresponding markings.

<td>Horses can no longer suffocate in the obsidian frame after going through <a href="/w/Nether_portal" class="mw-redirect" title="Nether portal">nether portals</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-12"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></td></tr><tr><th class="nowrap" rowspan="1" colspan="3"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_1.19.4" title="Java Edition 1.19.4">1.19.4</a></th><th colspan="4" rowspan="1"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_23w07a" title="Java Edition 23w07a">23w07a</a></th>
<td>When breeding horses and the like, the babies' speed, jump height, and health are now a variation of the average of the parents' stats. <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r3751077"><table class="wikitable pixel-image" data-description="History"><tbody><tr class="collapsible collapsible-rows"><th class="historytable-subheader" colspan="8" style="border-bottom: none"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_version_history" title="Java Edition version history"><i>Java Edition</i></a></th></tr><tr><th class="nowrap" rowspan="2" colspan="3"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_1.11" title="Java Edition 1.11">1.11</a></th><th colspan="4" rowspan="2"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_16w32a" title="Java Edition 16w32a">16w32a</a></th>
<td>The NBT <code>HasReproduced</code>, <code>Type</code> and <code>Saddle</code> has been removed
</td></tr><tr>
<td>Horses now have different IDs: <code>horse</code>, <code>donkey</code>, <code>mule</code>, <code>zombie_horse</code> and <code>skeleton_horse</code> <br> Note: Unused Variant IDs now result in a white horse rather than an invisible one.</td></tr><tr><th class="nowrap" rowspan="1" colspan="3"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_1.13" title="Java Edition 1.13">1.13</a></th><th colspan="4" rowspan="1"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_17w47a" title="Java Edition 17w47a">17w47a</a></th>
<td>Numeric IDs for entities were presumably deprecated in this version.​<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><a href="/w/Special:TalkPage/Horse" title="Special:TalkPage/Horse"><span title="what was this entity's numeric ID?" style="border-bottom: 1px dotted">more information needed</span></a></i>]</sup></td></tr><tr><th class="nowrap" rowspan="1" colspan="3"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_1.20.5" title="Java Edition 1.20.5">1.20.5</a></th><th colspan="4" rowspan="1"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_24w05a" title="Java Edition 24w05a">24w05a</a></th>
<td>Replaced <code>ArmorItem</code> tag with <code>body_armor_item</code>.</td></tr><tr><th class="nowrap" rowspan="2" colspan="3"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_1.21.5" title="Java Edition 1.21.5">1.21.5</a></th><th colspan="4" rowspan="2"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_25w03a" title="Java Edition 25w03a">25w03a</a></th>
<td>Replaced <code>body_armor_item</code> tag with <code>equipment.body</code>.
</td></tr><tr>
<td>Unified the NBT <code>SaddleItem</code> into the new <code>equipment.saddle</code> slot.</td></tr></tbody></table>
